Use only if clearly needed; neonatal EPS/withdrawal in 3rd trimester
Avoid; excreted in milk, infant sedation
BP, ECG/QTc, CBC, LFTs, EPS/tardive dyskinesia
summary: Chlorpromazine is the prototypical aliphatic phenothiazine antipsychotic, also used for nausea/vomiting, intractable hiccups, acute intermittent porphyria and behavioral disturbances. It is strongly sedating with prominent anticholinergic, alpha-blocking (hypotension) and QT-prolonging effects. It carries the class warning of increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis.
indications: Manic phase of bipolar disorder; control of severe agitation/hyperactivity

dosage.d: 30-75 mg/day initially in divided doses; increase to 200-800 mg/day
dosage.n: Severe/hospitalized may need higher; use lowest effective dose

dosage.d: 25 mg IM, may repeat 25-50 mg in 1 hour
dosage.n: Switch to oral when controlled; watch for hypotension

dosage.d: 10-25 mg PO q4-6h or 25 mg IM

dosage.n: Antiemetic/behavioral; caps by age/weight per label

dosage.d: 25-50 mg three to four times daily
dosage.n: IV route reserved for refractory cases under monitoring

admin: Avoid skin contact with solution/tablets (contact dermatitis)
Give IM deep into upper outer quadrant; keep patient supine and monitor BP
Do not give IV undiluted for routine use; reserve closely monitored IV
Use lowest effective dose; titrate gradually
Discontinue gradually to avoid withdrawal dyskinesia
moa: Chlorpromazine blocks postsynaptic dopamine D2 receptors in mesolimbic and other CNS pathways, producing antipsychotic and antiemetic (chemoreceptor trigger zone) effects. It also has potent antihistaminic, anticholinergic and alpha-1 adrenergic blocking activity, accounting for sedation, anticholinergic effects and orthostatic hypotension.

absolute: Comatose states or severe CNS depression
Concomitant large doses of CNS depressants
relative: Hepatic impairment / history of cholestatic jaundice
Narrow-angle glaucoma, prostatic hypertrophy, paralytic ileus

preg: Use only if clearly needed. Third-trimester exposure can cause neonatal extrapyramidal and/or withdrawal symptoms (agitation, hypertonia, feeding difficulty); monitor the newborn.
lact: Avoid. Chlorpromazine is excreted in breast milk and may cause drowsiness in the infant.
renal: Use with caution; monitor for accumulation of effects. No precise renal dosing defined.
hepatic: Use with caution; can cause cholestatic jaundice and is hepatically metabolized. Avoid in significant impairment and discontinue if jaundice develops.

major: Other QT-prolonging drugs - additive arrhythmia/torsades risk
CNS depressants/opioids/alcohol - additive sedation and respiratory depression
moderate: Anticholinergics - additive anticholinergic effects, paralytic ileus, hyperthermia
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; additive CNS depression and hypotension.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive urine pregnancy and phenylketonuria tests; prolongs QTc; may interfere with urinary steroid and porphyrin assays.

common: Dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation, urinary retention
rare: Skin/eye pigmentation, lens/corneal deposits with chronic use
emergency: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (hyperthermia, rigidity, autonomic instability)

monitoring: Blood pressure (orthostatic hypotension), especially with IM/IV use
ECG (QTc) and electrolytes in at-risk patients
Assess for EPS, tardive dyskinesia and NMS
counsel: Avoid alcohol and other sedating medicines
Avoid skin contact with the liquid/tablet
Report fever with muscle stiffness, uncontrolled movements, yellowing of skin/eyes, or fainting
pk: Sedation within ~30-60 min (IM faster than oral)
Store at 20-25 C, protect from light; do not freeze solution
pearls: Prototype phenothiazine - very sedating with strong anticholinergic and alpha-blocking effects
Marked orthostatic hypotension, especially after IM/IV - keep patient supine
Avoid epinephrine for chlorpromazine-induced hypotension (paradoxical further drop)
Useful for intractable hiccups and acute intermittent porphyria
Class warning: increased mortality in elderly dementia patients
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered unless it is close to the next dose; then skip it. Do not double up.
overdose: Overdose causes profound CNS depression, hypotension, extrapyramidal symptoms, QT prolongation and arrhythmias, seizures and hypo/hyperthermia. Provide supportive care with cardiac and BP monitoring; manage hypotension without epinephrine; treat arrhythmias cautiously. Dialysis is not effective. Activated charcoal may help early.
